$comment: RLS-9 ratchet (scripts/audit-rls-surface.ts). Call sites that read or write an RLS-covered table without a threaded transaction. The gate fails BOTH for an unlisted finding and for a listed entry whose count drops or disappears, so every entry is a deliberate, reviewable act with a diagnosed reason. Never add one merely to go green — see the header of scripts/audit-rls-surface.ts.
$baseline: 2026-08-25 — 34 sites, seeded from a LINE-ENDING-NORMALISED scan. The first CI run disagreed with the local one (32 vs 34): several detectors inspect a fixed CHARACTER window (400 chars after a call, 900 either side of db.execute), and CRLF costs one extra char per line, so a window spans fewer LINES on a Windows checkout than on Linux CI. The script now normalises CRLF before scanning, so both platforms agree.
$rls8: 2026-09-13 — RLS-8 triaged every entry: 17 sites remain, and none is untriaged. Each is either DELIBERATE (a write the NULL-safe policy permits with no tenant, or an anonymous read the policy itself carves out) or a verified FALSE POSITIVE (the detector is textual and the table actually queried has no policy). Everything that was a real bypass was scoped or routed through the admin path, and those entries are gone. A new finding here is therefore a regression, not backlog.
$howToTriage: Three legitimate outcomes per entry: (1) scope it — thread `tx` or wrap in withCurrentTenant; (2) route it through the RLS-6/RLS-7 adminDb path if it is a deliberate cross-tenant admin read; (3) keep it and document why, if it is a bootstrap path that must run before a tenant is known (token-authenticated lookups, login by email). Detection is TEXTUAL, so a false positive is also a valid reason — record that too.

allow.reason: DELIBERATE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). Registration: the transaction that creates the new user. A just-registered user has NO tenant, and `users`' WITH CHECK is `tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM app_current_tenant()`, so a NULL-tenant insert is permitted with nothing pinned — and pinning any tenant would reject it. The tenant is assigned later through withTenantAsUser.

DELIBERATE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). The bare insert is the NULL-tenant branch only — a genuine system event with no tenant anywhere; tenant-bearing entries are written through withTenant above it. `audit_logs`' policy is NULL-safe, so the insert is permitted with nothing pinned.

DELIBERATE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). Same shape as auditLogger.ts: `resolvedTenantId ? withTenant(...) : db.insert(...)` — the bare insert runs only when there is no tenant, which the NULL-safe policy permits.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). The db.* calls touch `mfa_secrets` / `mfa_backup_codes`, neither of which carries a policy. The detector catches the word `users` in the RLS-5 comments within 400 chars; the `users` writes themselves already go through the self-identification helpers.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-08-25. The call at line 639 is `db.select().from(templates)`, and `templates` has NO policy — it was deliberately removed from RLS_REPOS as a false positive (see this script's header). The db-call detector scans 400 chars after the call for a covered table name and catches `activeWorkflows`/`pinnedWorkflows` six lines below. Only surfaces on LF checkouts, where the window spans more lines — which is how it slipped past the Windows-seeded baseline.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). The call is `db.select().from(workflowVersions)`, and `workflow_versions` has no policy. The detector catches the step/page vocabulary in the surrounding final-block lookup.
FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). The call is a `SELECT 1` connectivity ping; it names no table. The 900-char window catches `users` in the neighbouring repository methods.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). The query reads `workflow_run_events`, which has no policy (same table as DropoffService). The window catches `workflow_id` / workflow vocabulary around it.

FALSE POSITIVE, verified 2026-08-25. Both db.execute() calls query `workflow_run_events`, which carries NO policy — it is not in COVERED_TABLES_SQL and has no CREATE POLICY in any migration. The raw-execute detector looks 900 chars either side of the call, and that window catches the word `workflows` from neighbouring SQL. Kept listed rather than narrowing the window, because a tighter window trades a false positive for a false negative, and this detector is the last line of defence for raw SQL. Re-verify if the query changes.

DELIBERATE, verified 2026-09-13 (RLS-8). Anonymous lookups of a workflow by public slug — there is no tenant to pin. Migration 0031's carve-out (`is_public = true AND status = 'active'` is visible with no tenant) is what makes them readable, and it means the database itself hides drafts and private workflows. Pinning a tenant would break them.
